candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies client-needs subcategory (13–19% of items); this item tests medication-related laboratory monitoring and recognition of serious adverse effects.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Medication laboratory monitoring and recognition of serious hematologic adverse effects
candidate.educational_objective: Obtain baseline hematologic testing before carbamazepine and closely evaluate declining white blood cell or platelet counts because clinically significant bone-marrow suppression, including rare aplastic anemia or agranulocytosis, can occur.

options.A: Carbamazepine has been associated with aplastic anemia, agranulocytosis, and other decreases in blood-cell counts that can signal significant bone-marrow depression
options.B: Carbamazepine predictably increases white blood cells and platelets, so falling counts indicate the medication is working
options.C: Hematologic abnormalities are unrelated to carbamazepine and do not require follow-up during therapy
options.D: Every minor blood-count change means aplastic anemia is present and requires automatic discontinuation

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current DailyMed carbamazepine labeling contains a boxed warning that aplastic anemia and agranulocytosis have been reported. It directs complete pretreatment hematologic testing as a baseline and states that if white blood cell or platelet counts become low or decrease during treatment, the client should be monitored closely; discontinuation should be considered if significant bone-marrow depression develops. B and C contradict the label. D is too absolute because the label specifically notes that most minor hematologic changes do not progress to aplastic anemia or agranulocytosis and does not mandate automatic discontinuation for every minor change.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The current official carbamazepine label directly supports baseline hematologic testing and close follow-up of falling white blood cell or platelet counts because of clinically important bone-marrow suppression risk, while explicitly rejecting the assumption that every minor count change equals aplastic anemia or agranulocytosis.
candidate.source_document_title: TEGRETOL (carbamazepine) tablets, suspension, and extended-release tablets
candidate.source_locator: DailyMed current TEGRETOL label → Boxed Warning 'Aplastic Anemia and Agranulocytosis': these reactions have been reported; most minor hematologic changes do not progress to these serious disorders; obtain complete pretreatment hematologic testing as a baseline; if white blood cell or platelet counts are low or decrease during treatment, monitor closely; consider discontinuation if significant bone-marrow depression develops.
candidate.source_organization: National Library of Medicine (DailyMed; FDA-approved prescribing information)
candidate.stem: A client is starting carbamazepine. Why is pretreatment hematologic testing obtained and why should a decline in white blood cells or platelets during therapy be followed closely?
